finding.text: `core/doc/status.md` is not in the diff: line 14 still lists "the `unset` verb" under "Not built", and line 49 still lists it as next. Requirement 7 asks for it to be updated as each item lands.

The task folder has no record of the merge gate (requirement 6). `session.jsonl` logs the plan and two commits, but no `ReplayCompare` result (records compared, differences) and no `run-all.mjs` result. A fresh agent can't tell whether item 1 passed the gate. Log both results before merging.

`Template.unset(name)` (`core/Page/Template/Template.js:83`) now overrides `Item.unset`. On a Template, `set({k: undefined})` (`Item.js:281`) and a replayed `{"unset":[…]}` line call the Template's map version, which saves no line and is given an array. `doc/line-format.md` says the Template version "keeps its own meaning", but this side effect is not written down. A Template is probably never stored, so this is low risk.

`unset()` deletes from `this.data` directly and checks `Object.hasOwn(this.data, key)` (`Item.js:147`). It skips the `get_one`/`put` seams that `Ref.put` and Panel's master/mirror reads depend on. Unsetting a shared key on a Panel mirror writes nothing, and `Ref.changes` is not bumped when `path`/`url` is cleared. That is fine for now; it's worth one sentence in the doc.
The scope matches plan item 1 only, which fits "one merge per item". Items 2–5 are still open, and `plan.md` plus `reset-epoch/requirements.md` hold enough for a fresh agent to continue.

In `core/doc/status.md:14` the new `unset` and unknown-key sentences sit straight after "Built but off: *writing* the new spelling…", with no "Done:" label of their own. A quick reader could take `unset` as built-but-off; starting them with "Also done (2026-11-02):" would fix that.

Requirement 2 says "unknown bare keys", but the check is narrower (`Item.js:303`, `unknown_key` at `Item.js:87`). It only reports an object value, read from a log, on a List or a list member. A bare key on a root record (a session or task file's top level) is never reported. `doc/line-format.md` explains this and gives the census (27 false alarms down to 4 real ones), so this is a fair reading of the ask, not a miss.

`Item.calling` (`Item.js:117`) is one global counter, not one per store. While any line's method call runs, every unknown key is silenced, and an explicit `{"set":…}` line counts as a method call. That is the intent (doc, "Not reported"). It also means a newer writer's verb inside a `set` line is never caught.

Node scripts that replay every record (`ReplayCompare`, the item tool) now print up to 4 `unknown:` warnings, one per key, on today's records. Expected and documented; just don't mistake them for a regression.

`diff.patch` still holds merge 1 (`unset`, already landed as 244efeaab) as well as merge 2. Both were checked. The earlier review's two fixes are in: status.md is updated, and the gate is logged in `session.jsonl`.

`item.batch(fn)` keeps lines only in memory for as long as `fn` awaits: held lines sit in `Store._queue` and reach the Outbox (which survives a reload) only on `release()` (`core/Item/Store.js`, `hold`/`release`). If the tab is closed or reloaded during the await (e.g. the `save_picture()` upload in `doc/batch.md`), those lines are lost and nothing warns. Before, they were sent within one microtask. This is the kind of silent loss Phase 0 was meant to stop. Fix: on `pagehide`/hidden, flush held stores the way `Store.flush_typing` already does for typing, and add a sentence about it to `doc/batch.md`.

The `Task.wait()` line count disagrees between files. `batch.test.mjs:6` and the test name at `batch.test.mjs:64` say "1, not 7". `doc/batch.md`, the readme, `status.md` and the session log say "not 8". Use one number.
`core/doc/status.md` row 1 still says "**About half**", but only typing coalesce and `Room` + `FileJournal` are left. The headline should say how much is actually done.
`Item.source` sits between `static get clock()` and `static set clock()` (Item.js, diff line 57–62), which splits the getter from its setter. Move it below `set clock`.

The `"read"` event's listeners now run under `Store.replay_depth++` (Store.js ~line 258). That turns off saving for every store, not just this one. The current listeners are fine: Ref.settle only emits, and SessionTasks and DefaultView defer or only draw. But a future `"read"` listener that writes to another file will be dropped without any warning. `doc/batch.md` says this only for "this" store, so it should say the mute is global.

`Store.merge` copies `set` keys in the order they were first inserted. A key that is set, then given a dotted sub-key, then set again would replay in the wrong order. Today `set()` never emits dotted keys inside `set`, so nothing breaks yet.

The gate log says `run-all` gave 218/219. The one failure is `Servex/whisper-detach.test.mjs`, which passes alone and touches no Item code. The brief asks for a clean `run-all` before each merge, so record that exception in the landing line.

The hold applies to every data line in a browser, not just typing: a single `set()` from a click (a task status, a checkbox) now reaches the file up to 300 ms later (`core/Item/Store.js` `typing()`). A button that sets a field and then asks Servex or an agent to read that file at once could read the old state. I found no caller that waits on `store.pending` or `flush()`, so nothing breaks today. The alternative the doc records ("send the first keystroke at once", `doc/batch.md` Caveat) would remove this delay.

On page hide, typing is flushed through `end_typing()`, which queues the flush on a microtask. `send_held()` instead calls `flush()` synchronously (`Store.js` `listen_for_hide`). Both should run before unload, but making `flush_typing` call `flush()` directly, as `send_held` does, would put both on the same path that the batch review fix already chose.
The first test is titled "ten keystrokes" but types "hello there", which is 11 (`coalesce.test.mjs:30`). `doc/batch.md` correctly says 11.

`batch.test.mjs` sets `Store.coalesce = null` for the whole module and never restores it. That's fine while each test file opens as its own page. If two files ever share one browser page, the setting leaks into the second one.
